evidence: The provisional Design provides closed failure signals, fail-closed telemetry and terminal recovery, bounded identifiers, and actionable rollback paths. Its critical native event wait is not deadline-bounded, so loss of completion/attention events can strand the wave past the accepted eight-hour stop boundary.

findings.issue: The critical native event wait is specified as long-lived and wakeable only by completion or attention, but it has no absolute deadline or timeout-to-attention behavior when Codex event transport stops producing events.
findings.why: An outstanding worker or lost host event can leave delivery blocked indefinitely. The budget is checked before starts and names an eight-hour ceiling, but no event may arrive to return control and enforce that ceiling, so the new host dependency has an unbounded failure mode on the critical path.
findings.suggestion: Bind the single wait to the remaining absolute wave deadline, with the child deadline strictly earlier than the eight-hour ceiling; define expiry as one host-native attention outcome that records the outstanding-set fingerprint and elapsed/usage identities, stops for human scope review, and never reissues or polls automatically. Add a selector where completion and attention transport are silent and prove the deadline path returns bounded failure before the ceiling.
